subject: Tempered cutover timeline and integration checkmatrix for LedgerWorks RFP
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@ledgerworks.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Detailed migration & cutover questionnaire — LedgerWorks RFP

Jonas —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. As part of our RFP evaluation we'd like a detailed migration / cutover questionnaire that covers timeline, integration sequencing, canary windows, rollback criteria, and validation checks. Specifically we need:

- A phase-by-phase timeline from preflight to full cutover
- Integration steps for our ledger sync and payment rails (including dual-write expectations)
- Canary schedule and success criteria (metrics, duration, traffic % thresholds)
- Data validation and reconciliation steps (pre/post checks)
- Explicit rollback/fallback procedures and expected RTO/RPO
- Required network and security steps (IP ranges, cert rotations, firewall changes)

Can you send a draft runbook and a short checklist matrix that we can share with our infra and security teams? Preferably by EOD Tuesday.

Appreciate it —
Alice Monroe
VP Product, LedgerWorks
---
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@ledgerworks.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 13:40:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed migration & cutover questionnaire — LedgerWorks RFP

Alice —

Thanks for the clear ask. I've put together a draft high-level plan and an attached checklist (tempered-cutover-draft-v1.pdf) that maps the phases to owners and acceptance criteria. Summary below — full draft attached.

1) Preflight (1–2 weeks pre-cutover)
   - Network & security: whitelist Redwood egress IPs, exchange cert fingerprints, confirm KMS access patterns
   - Preflight sync: initial bulk import + differential pass; data quality checks (row counts, hash checks)
   - Smoke tests in staging using representative traffic (10k synthetic transactions)

2) Canary (preferred 48–72 hour window)
   - Canary epoch 1 (low-risk): 1% production traffic, 30–60 minute sustained stability check
   - Canary epoch 2 (scale): 10% traffic, 4-hour observation with latency/p99 and error-rate SLAs
   - Success criteria: error rate < 0.3%, tail latency within 1.5x baseline, reconciliation delta < 0.05%

3) Gradual ramp (3–7 days)
   - 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% with operational gates at each step and automated rollback hooks

4) Full cutover & verification (1–2 days)
   - Run end-to-end reconciliation queries, compare hashes, promote model configs, confirm billing metrics

Fallback lanes: immediate traffic diversion to existing endpoints; automated disable of write path + queued retry approach for any partial failures. Expected RTO: 15–30 minutes for traffic diversion; RPO depends on last successful checkpoint (typically sub-minute with dual-write).

Open items: confirm exact maintenance window preferences (timezone), whether LedgerWorks requires an airgap for audit logs, and who will own runbook sign-off during canary.

I'll loop in Sales and Solutions to add the integration checkmatrix and monitoring hooks. Can we schedule a 60-minute runbook workshop on Tue or Wed?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: tempered-cutover-draft-v1.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:15:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed migration & cutover questionnaire — LedgerWorks RFP

Jonas —

This is a good structure. A couple of practical items for the RFP response: 

- Add explicit acceptance criteria tied to billing (we should note expected token/ingest impacts during ramp)
- Recommend Canary windows align to their low-traffic period (ask: do they have preferred PST windows?)
- Suggest an initial production canary of 2 hours min (rather than 30–60m) to account for third-party downstreams

I'll draft a short commercial caveat paragraph for the final doc (limits on SLA during ramp) — Aditya, can you add the technical validation checklist (endpoints, auth scopes, sample queries) so we can include an appendix?

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Enterprise Sales
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 11:02:09 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed migration & cutover questionnaire — LedgerWorks RFP

Laura / Jonas —

Attached is a technical checkmatrix (integration-checkmatrix.xlsx) with step-by-step tasks and verification commands. High-level additions I recommend putting in the runbook: 

- Network: add specific egress IP ranges and FQDNs (redwood-ingest.redwood.ai), TLS cert fingerprints, and one-hour cert-rotation contingency
- Auth: OAuth client-id exchange + short-lived tokens for the canary; fallback to API key for emergency rollback
- Data sync: two-phase sync — bulk import (S3 -> staging) followed by differential CDC stream; keep CDC lag < 30s during canary
- KV cache priming: pre-warm caches for the top 5K hot keys before moving traffic to reduce p99 spikes
- Monitoring hooks: preconfigured dashboards (prometheus: redwood/cutover, grafana: ledgerworks-cutover) and alert thresholds (error_rate > 0.25% for 5m)
- Operational commands: documented curl commands and scripts for disabling writes, toggling read replicas, and extracting reconciliation exports

I included suggested queries for reconciliation (sample SQLs) and a short checklist for security to verify log forwarding and KMS access.

Attachments: integration-checkmatrix.xlsx

- Aditya
Solutions Engineer
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@ledgerworks.com>
Cc: Marco Silva <marco.silva@ledgerworks.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Detailed migration & cutover questionnaire — LedgerWorks RFP

Alice / Marco —

Thanks again for the ask. Please find attached a consolidated runbook bundle (tempered-cutover-final.zip) that includes: the draft plan with ownership table, the integration-checkmatrix.xlsx, preflight checklist, monitoring dashboard links, and the rollback playbook. Key callouts in this consolidated copy: 

- Proposed initial canary window: 2027-10-12 02:00–06:00 PT (we recommend starting on a Tue/Wed overnight window)
- Canary gating: automated rollback if any one of (error_rate > 0.3% for 10m, p99 latency > 1.5x baseline for 10m, reconciliation delta > 0.05%)
- Operational contact list & escalation ladder included in appendix

Next steps: please confirm the maintenance window and provide the infra owner's contact so we can schedule the runbook workshop (we'll include a dry-run checklist). Once we have sign-off we'll assign a runbook owner and lock down the timeline in the SOW.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
